answer: Divergent-Trace Registration. Each identity must submit a unique recent interaction trace rooted in a shared public wharf log. Clones derive identical traces, so their signatures cluster within a tight delta; the registry admits at most one identity per cluster per epoch. An attacker cloning N identities gains one admission, and must generate N genuinely distinct live traces—paying full interaction cost N times—while a failed cluster audit forfeits that cluster's atlas slot.
